notes: Claude Code, through `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` 0.100.0 (the Claude Agent SDK underneath). Its fence  goes in `_meta.claudeCode.options` (`settings`, `sandbox`, `disallowedTools`), written once its gates pass. Unmeasured (from docs, `--help` and code, S5 §3): where a row isn't known it takes the cautious value (a reattach by `load` with its replay dropped, MCP names unread, calls a cancel leaves open closed by MOSS), it is held as acting without asking (`unasked-actions`) since it loads the user's own approval settings, and no sandbox is admitted, so it asks for the user's OK. The agent suite's live gates measure each row. The adapter's `--version` may name its package (`@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp <n>`); the older `@zed-industries/claude-agent-acp` (0.23.x) answers nothing and is not started. MOSS provides the adapter itself (`launch.adapter`): 0.100.0 and the 106 packages it needs (`adapter-lock.json`, made by `scripts/agent-adapter-lock.ts` from npm's lockfile; each hash from the public registry's metadata), fetched behind one card, checked against its integrity before it is unpacked, and run on MOSS's own Bun. It drives the user's own `claude`, which MOSS finds and hands it in `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE` (the vendor SDK's own 300 MB native binary is not fetched). The user's own installed adapter is the fallback while MOSS's copy isn't there.
